title: Quiz: Lean Six Sigma — Waste Elimination and Quality Tools

questions.text: A hospital triage process has a total lead time of 80 minutes, of which 18 minutes are value-added. What is the process efficiency?
questions.explanation: Process Efficiency = (VA time / Total lead time) × 100 = (18 / 80) × 100 = 22.5%. The remaining 77.5% of elapsed time is non-value-added waste from the customer's perspective.

questions.text: In the TIMWOODS mnemonic, which waste category describes producing more output than the customer currently needs?
questions.explanation: Overproduction means making more, sooner, or faster than required. It is considered the most harmful waste in lean thinking because it generates all other wastes — excess inventory, additional transport, more waiting, and more motion.

questions.text: A Value Stream Map (VSM) records cycle time (CT) and inventory (I) at each process step. What is the primary purpose of creating a VSM 'current state' map?
options: To make flow and waste visible so improvement priorities can be identified
To replace control charts as the primary SPC monitoring tool
To document product specifications for the customer
To count the number of defects per million opportunities
questions.explanation: The current-state VSM makes the entire material and information flow visible — including all waiting, transport, and inventory between steps. This visibility is the foundation for identifying which wastes to eliminate in the future-state design.

questions.text: In the 5S methodology, which step involves creating written standards so that Sort, Set in Order, and Shine are performed consistently?
questions.explanation: Standardise (Seiketsu) is the 4th S — it establishes documented procedures and visual controls so that the first three Ss are performed consistently by all team members at all times, creating the conditions needed for Sustain.

questions.text: Lean Six Sigma combines lean's focus on flow speed and waste removal with Six Sigma's focus on reducing process variation and defect rates.
questions.explanation: Lean and Six Sigma are complementary. Lean eliminates waste to compress lead times and improve flow, while Six Sigma reduces variation and defects within the remaining value-adding steps. Lean Six Sigma integrates both under the DMAIC improvement structure.
